text.en: A teashop owner at a Garhwal bus stop tells a stranger his own story over a hot cup of tea.

The narrator, Brij, is a seventeen-year-old who runs a small tea shop on the road to Badrinath in Garhwal. He greets a tired traveller and invites him to warm up at the shop while he makes tea. As he talks, he tells about his work and about an earthquake that changed the place and his life.
The story is told in the first person, in a friendly, direct way as if Brij speaks to you. It reminds us to help others, especially in hard times, and shows how young people can be responsible and brave. The warm-up question asks when you last helped someone.
Look at the conversational words such as Greetings, traveller, Sir and My name. Learn nouns like pilgrim, valley and teashop. (Written from the opening of the story in the textbook; read the full text in your book for the events of the earthquake.)
